label: rare: <DEL> or copied l/2 at steps 8-12 (context-specific, low precision)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.024% of steps). About 96% of activation mass is in the delimiter/copy phase, mostly at absolute steps 8-12 and in long sequences (L=9 holds about half the mass). The input token is almost always <DEL> (26% of mass), a copied l (45%) or a copied 2 (14%), with some w/z; it is essentially silent during the original phase. The strongest activations are on <DEL> in L=9 sequences, often where the last original token is h/i and the first token is w/l, sometimes spilling onto the first copied token w. But only a tiny fraction of matching steps fire: <DEL>/l/2 at steps 8-12 covers 76% of mass at 0.4% precision, and the best F1 any predicate reached (copied l at steps 8-12) was 0.025. Adding prev_tok, first_tok or L conditions did not raise precision above about 4%. Activation magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.12, max 0.23) and no tested variable clearly modulated it. Whatever decides firing seems to depend on the whole sequence context, and the per-step variables available do not capture it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=l (+5.09), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+4.13), phase=2 & out_tok=r (+3.28), phase=2 & in_tok=z (+3.15), out_tok=l (+2.80), phase=2 & in_tok=w (+2.77). Lower it: next_out=- (-2.93), phase=2 (-2.93), orig1=i (-2.48), orig0=i (-2.04).
